evals.name: split-unrelated-changes
evals.prompt: I fixed the bug where shipped orders could still be cancelled, and while I was in there I fixed a typo in the README. Commit it.
evals.expected_output: Two commits, not one: a fix(orders) commit for orders.py and a docs commit for README.md, each with a conventional subject.

files.README.md:
# Shop

A tiny order service.

## Instal

Run `pip install -e .`

# Shop

A tiny order service.

## Install

Run `pip install -e .`

expectations: Exactly two new commits were created: one touching only orders.py and one touching only README.md
The orders.py commit subject uses type fix with the orders scope, e.g. fix(orders): ...
The README.md commit subject uses type docs
Every new commit subject is imperative, lowercase after the type prefix, has no trailing period, and is at most 72 characters
The working tree is clean afterwards: git status shows no changes and no leftover commit-message file

evals.name: breaking-change-with-issue
evals.prompt: I renamed get_user to fetch_user and made include_deleted keyword-only, so callers will have to update. This is for issue #58 in our tracker and it should close when merged. Please commit.
evals.expected_output: One commit marked breaking (! or BREAKING CHANGE footer) with migration notes and a Closes #58 footer, written via git commit -F.
expectations: Exactly one new commit was created and it touches only api.py
The commit is marked breaking: a ! after the type/scope in the subject, a BREAKING CHANGE: footer, or both
The commit message tells callers how to migrate: call fetch_user instead of get_user and pass include_deleted by keyword
The commit message has a footer line reading exactly `Closes #58`
The transcript shows the multi-line message was passed with git commit -F <file>, not a shell heredoc, a PowerShell here-string, or several -m flags
No temporary commit-message file is left in the working tree

evals.name: scope-from-history
evals.prompt: commit the discount thing i just added
evals.expected_output: One feat(billing) commit whose subject names the discount, reusing the scope already in git log for this directory.

files.billing/invoice.py:
def total(lines):
    return sum(qty * price for qty, price in lines)

expectations: Exactly one new commit was created and it touches only billing/invoice.py
The subject uses type feat and scope billing, matching the scope git log already uses for this directory
The subject names the discount specifically rather than a vague 'update invoice'
The subject is imperative, lowercase after the type prefix, has no trailing period, and is at most 72 characters
